angleRead.text: The dossier gives me three seasons of Vladimir Gonzalez and one peer season from Frank Reyna, and the order you read them in changes the story. Read 2037 first — 16 games, 61 at-bats, a home run every 30.5 at-bats, a strikeout every 7.6 — and you see a young corner outfielder with pop and a swing that misses. Read 2038 next — 35 games, 120 at-bats, two home runs, one every 60 at-bats, a strikeout every 4.8 — and the pop looks like it vanished while the whiff rate got worse. Then read 2039, the full season, 127 games, 506 at-bats, 14 home runs, one every 36.1 at-bats, a strikeout every 6.5 — and the power is back to roughly where it started, the strikeout rate improved, and the batting averag

plan.chase: The dossier gives me three seasons of Vladimir Gonzalez and one peer season from Frank Reyna, and the order you read them in changes the story. Read 2037 first — 16 games, 61 at-bats, a home run every 30.5 at-bats, a strikeout every 7.6 — and you see a young corner outfielder with pop and a swing that misses. plan.focus: Vladimir Gonzalez's 2039 full-season line as the reliable estimate of his true power and contact rates, against the thin-sample 2038 season and the peer band set by Frank Reyna's 2041.
plan.why: The 2038 season is the trap — 120 at-bats is too small to carry meaning, but it is the season that would get cited in a roster debate. The 2039 season, at 506 at-bats, is the evidence. The peer comparison keeps the claim honest: it does not overstate Gonzalez.
plan.interpretation: The 2038 season is the hinge. It is the smallest sample and the worst line. The 2039 season, on a full-year sample, restores the power rate to roughly the 2037 level and improves the strikeout rate. The peer band from Reyna shows what elite production at the position looks like — and Gonzalez is not that. He is a solid everyday corner outfielder, not a star. The claim is that the 2039 line is the identity, and the 2038 line is noise.
unverifiedLead: Whether Gonzalez's 2040 season, when it arrives, keeps the home run rate near one per 36 at-bats or drifts toward the 2038 rate — that is the number that would confirm or kill the claim.
plan.closeQuestion: Does the 2040 season, on a full-year sample, hold the home run rate above one per 50 at-bats and the strikeout rate below one per 5?
